extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, and informed general readers seeking critical reviews of scientific and technical books)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative points used by a reviewer to judge scientific and technical books (coverage, accuracy, illustrations, audience suitability, methods, bibliography, production quality, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and coverage (title fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must be interpreted correctly and the content should match the scope implied; e.g., 'The title of Dr. Aitchison’s book must be interpreted in a rather restricted sense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the subjects the intended readers expect (e.g., steels used for ship and boiler plates, rails, girders) are actually treated; note if the work is largely confined to a narrower subset (automobile and aircraft steels) than the title suggests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence and breadth of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should make adequate reference to relevant evidence and literatures; 'The present volume would have gained by a wider reference to evidence derived from ethnological sources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether comparative sources and pertinent fields are consulted; note presence or absence of references to original sources and whether bibliographies are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific accuracy and terminological precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'termino-zoological inexactitudes' and other taxonomic or disciplinary confusions that 'tend somewhat to obscure the scientific status of the book.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for correct classification, accurate use of technical terms (e.g., distinguishing bony fishes from cartilaginous rays), and sound handling of domain-specific distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, readability and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing should be 'light-hearted, attractive, and unpedantic' or 'easy and readable throughout' when appropriate for the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prose style, whether the author writes clearly and engagingly, and whether tone matches purpose (e.g., accessible for general readers vs. technical for specialists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate technical level and audience suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The book should match the knowledge level of its intended readers: 'the work is not intended for the expert' / 'they demand a previous knowledge of classification and external morphology'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if the text assumes prerequisite knowledge or is accessible to non-specialists; check whether it is suitable for engineers, students, the average member, or specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and figures: quality and quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should be 'good and numerous' when needed; conversely, 'figures and charts are indispensable' and too few or poor diagrams (e.g., 'only eight text-figures and these are rather difficult diagrams') hinder comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both the number and clarity of illustrations/figures and whether they effectively support the text (especially in topics requiring visual data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Material should be coherently organized; avoid producing a 'curious mosaic of random thoughts' that may confuse readers unfamiliar with the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether chapters and sections cohere into a sustained argument or present a confusing scatter of impressions; note where sustained discussion exists versus episodic anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative judgment and practical experience
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's practical experience can greatly enhance value: 'the author has brought to bear upon his task the experience of a practical and enthusiastic angler.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the author's field experience and whether that experience strengthens descriptions, habits, and applied recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between practical instruction and theoretical depth
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be an appropriate balance: e.g., 'Moulding is considered much more fully than melting' and 'the theoretical side is weak' are criticisms when theory is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether practical descriptions are supported by adequate theoretical explanation and whether simplifications (e.g., of heat treatment) are misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness and practical applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A work's utility to practitioners and students is important: 'should be in the possession of all surveyors who intend to proceed there' / 'should be in the hands of all students of marine biology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book provides actionable guidance, methods, or summaries that practitioners and students can use in the field or laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor and worked examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed methods and worked examples are valuable: 'the method of obtaining the true meridian by single observations on the sun is clearly and fully explained, with the aid of several worked examples.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clear statement of methods, inclusion of worked examples or experimental descriptions, and practical instruction for applying techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography, references and bibliographical care
rubrics_metrics.description: A meticulous bibliography and bibliographical research add value: 'prepared ... with the same meticulous care and accuracy' and 'a full bibliography of papers relating to the determination of hardness is given.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness and accuracy of references, presence of addenda/corrigenda, and usefulness of bibliographical material for researchers (priority, citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and coverage of recent research
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should reflect recent developments where relevant: 'the whole subject ... is in a state of flux' and 'no such work ... includes all the recent investigations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether the text incorporates up-to-date findings, whether authoritative statements are premature in a changing field, and where key recent work is omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical production quality (printing and binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production values matter: 'The book is very well printed and illustrated' but it is 'a pity that so valuable a work ... should have been sent out in a paper cover.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess printing quality, quality of plates/photographs, and suitability of binding/cover for long-term use and library preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of illustrative cases and practical records
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of case records and illustrative examples increases usefulness: 'a number of illustrative cases from the records of various doctors are given' for snake-bite treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether case studies or records are provided and whether they aid practitioners (medical, fieldworkers, engineers) in applying knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative and ethnological data for interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative/ethnological evidence strengthens historical or archaeological interpretation: 'Ethnological data must be brought to bear upon archaeological research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for cross-cultural comparisons and ethnological sources when interpreting ancient practices or artifacts; note missed opportunities to use such data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasiveness and handling of controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments and interpretations should be persuasive and fairly treated: reviewer notes author 'revels in argument' yet sometimes 'fails to be entirely convincing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well controversies are presented, whether competing theories are fairly quoted and evaluated, and whether the author's own position is convincingly argued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and defensibility of taxonomic or nomenclatural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to genus/species names or taxonomic judgments must be justified: 'Sometimes the generic and specific names have been altered. ... not always inspired with confidence in Col. Wall’s judgment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require careful justification and awareness of contested points when departing from established classifications; avoid dogmatic assertions without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and jurisdictional relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: A book's practical utility may vary by region: e.g., 'only the first three chapters are likely to be of much service to mine surveyors in England.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether methods, examples, legal/procedural material, or instruments described are applicable in other jurisdictions or only in the region treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of technical material for non-professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical books should consider non-professional readers: 'It can be read with advantage and by the non-professional reader only with constant reference to a good atlas', indicating insufficiently accessible diagrams or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether explanatory aids (atlases, glossaries, clear diagrams) are provided to make technical material usable by informed non-specialists.
